modules.behavior: UART 8N1 transmitter with a valid/ready byte input and a shortened stop bit, public parameter DIV=868 (clock cycles per bit; 868 gives 115200 baud from a 100 MHz clock), supported experiment domain integer DIV 16..4096. Define STOP = DIV - DIV/16 using integer division (814 at the default). Ports: in_data[7:0], in_valid, in_ready (output), tx (output, the serial line). Idle: tx=1 and in_ready=1. A byte is accepted at rising edge k when in_valid && in_ready && !rst; in_data is captured at that edge and later input changes are ignored until the frame ends. Bits are sent least significant data bit first: bit 0 is the start bit (0), bits 1..8 are in_data[0]..in_data[7], bit 9 is the stop bit (1). For i in 0..9, bit i is visible on tx after the NBA update of edge k+i*DIV. Bits 0..8 last exactly DIV cycles each; the stop bit lasts STOP cycles: after the NBA update of edge k+9*DIV+STOP the transmitter is idle again (tx=1, in_ready=1). The earliest next accept is edge k+9*DIV+STOP+1, so back-to-back frames repeat every 9*DIV+STOP+1 cycles (8627 at the default), which keeps up with a sender running up to 0.6% fast. in_ready is 0 from after edge k until that idle edge. in_valid while busy is ignored, not queued. tx and in_ready are registered outputs: they change only at rising edges, never combinationally from inputs or from rst. Synchronous active-high rst at a rising edge aborts any frame and returns to idle (tx=1, in_ready=1) and overrides an accept at the same edge; it has no effect between edges. The top uart_tx is the board configuration, fixed at the default DIV=868, and the trusted testbench checks the top only. For the Python golden model, each non-reset step is one clock edge with that step's inputs, returning tx and in_ready after the edge.

When known=false, absence of a top annotation is not a failed or unverifiable criterion. Unannotated numeric latency is UNKNOWN, not zero.
